in_text_mentions: Family RP19 was initially given a diagnosis of autosomal recessive RP. However, during fundoscopy of the individuals IV-3 and V-1, no bone spicule deposits were observed in the fundus (Figure 2A), which are typical for RP. Scotopic ERG showed a significantly reduced rod response (data not shown).

on of the fundus, which are characteristic signs of the disease. The typical Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon of fundus changes for Oguchi was observed in the affected individuals who were subjected to a dark adaptation of only 2 h. The normal recommended time of dark adaptation is at least 2–3 h to see a clear difference between the light and dark adapted fundus. The Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon in the participants of our study exhibited a less marked disappearance of the fundus' unusual gray discoloration and the appearance of the reddish coloration due to reduced time for dark adaptation (Figure 2B).

plate_findings.evidence: normal appearance after 2–3 h of dark adaptation

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Fundus photograph before dark adaptation showing the characteristic grayish-yellow/golden-brown discoloration of Oguchi disease. B: Fundus photograph after prolonged dark adaptation showing reversal of the abnormal fundus color, consistent with the Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon in Oguchi disease.
panels.attribution_text: Waheed et al. A nonsense mutation in S-antigen (p.Glu306*) causes Oguchi disease.. Molecular vision 2012. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Dark adaptation test of the patient. Fundus photographs of the patient before (A) and after (B) dark adaptation. The fundus appearance was characteristic of Oguchi disease with grayish-yellow discoloration that had normal appearance after 2–3 h of dark adaptation.
in_text_mentions: Ophthalmological examination showed that the uncorrected visual acuity of the patient (V:1) was 6/9 for both eyes. Ophthalmoscopy showed static hemeralopia (which is clinically correlated to the side effect of medication) with a grayish-yellow metallic sheen of the fundus in the peripheral area (Figure 2A). The photopic ERG was normal while the scotopic ERG of the patient showed significantly reduced rod response (data not shown). After prolonged dark adaptation, the grayish-yellow fundus appearance reverted to normal (Figure 2B), which is typical in patients with Oguchi disease.

findings.label: Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon on dark adaptation
findings.evidence: Color fundus photographs of the right eye ... after prolonged dark adaptation ... demonstrating the disappearance of the metallic golden fundus sheen and the restoration of a near-normal retinal appearance, consistent with the Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (Left panel, Right panel). Left panel: Human fundus photograph showing the post-dark-adaptation Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon in Oguchi disease. Right panel: Human fundus photograph showing the post-dark-adaptation Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon in Oguchi disease.
panels.attribution_text: Jaleel and Rasheed. The Golden Sheen Retina Fades by Dusk: An Incidental Adult Presentation of Oguchi Disease.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.112119. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon. Color fundus photographs of the right eye (left panel) and left eye (right panel) obtained after prolonged dark adaptation (approximately eight hours), demonstrating the disappearance of the metallic golden fundus sheen and the restoration of a near-normal retinal appearance, consistent with the Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon.
in_text_mentions: cal diagnosis of Oguchi disease. Although electroretinography (ERG), genetic testing, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), and fundus autofluorescence (FAF) were not performed, the diagnosis was considered to be strongly supported by the characteristic clinical findings. Fundus examination the following morning after pharmacologic dilation showed complete disappearance of the metallic sheen, with restoration of a near-normal retinal appearance (Figure 2). This reversible change represented the classic Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon, a pathognomonic feature of Oguchi disease [1-3].

plate_findings.evidence: severely reduced b-wave amplitude with a mild reduction of the a-wave

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: The panel displays an ERG tracing from a patient with Oguchi disease, showing severely reduced b-wave amplitude after 30 min of dark adaptation, which is a clear clinical manifestation. b: The panel displays an ERG tracing from a patient with Oguchi disease, showing improvement of amplitudes after 6 hours of dark adaptation, which is a characteristic feature documented in the case.
